quizzes.question: A powerful tidal bore known as the pororoca creates waves up to 13 feet high that travel up to 50 miles upstream along this body of water during full and new moons. Though recent studies point to the Mantaro River as its ultimate source, its primary source was traditionally identified as Nevado Mismi in the Peruvian Andes. Accounting for roughly 20 percent of total global river discharge, this river surprisingly has no bridges crossing its main stem. For the point, name this massive South American river, the largest in the world by discharge volume.
quizzes.explanation: The Amazon River features the pororoca tidal bore, originates in the Andes, has no bridges along its main stem, and holds the world's highest discharge volume.

quizzes.question: The time rate of change of this physical quantity itself is known in physics as 'jerk.' In uniform circular motion, its centripetal form maintains an object's trajectory by pointing directly toward the center of curvature with a magnitude equal to velocity squared divided by the radius. Defined as the second derivative of position with respect to time, it is directly proportional to net force according to Newton's Second Law. For the point, name this vector quantity that describes the rate of change of velocity over time.
quizzes.explanation: Acceleration is defined as the rate of change of velocity over time; its derivative with respect to time is jerk, and it is related to force by Newton's Second Law (F = ma).

quizzes.question: The summit of this physical feature continues to rise at a rate of approximately 4 millimeters per year due to the ongoing collision of the Indian and Eurasian tectonic plates. Climbers attempting to reach its summit must traverse the hazardous 'Death Zone' above 8,000 meters, where atmospheric pressure drops significantly and oxygen levels are insufficient to sustain human life long-term. First officially summited in 1953 by Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay, it is known locally as Sagarmatha in Nepal and Chomolungma in Tibet. For the point, name this peak in the Himalayas, the highest mountain above sea level on Earth.
quizzes.explanation: Mount Everest is Earth's highest peak above sea level at 8,848.86 meters, located on the border between Nepal and Tibet in the Himalayas.

quizzes.question: The interior of this cellular structure is supported by a fibrous network composed of intermediate filament proteins called lamins, known as the nuclear lamina. Its outer lipid bilayer is perforated by complex pores that regulate macromolecular transport, and it contains a dense sub-structure called the nucleolus responsible for transcribing ribosomal RNA. Containing DNA complexed with histone proteins to form chromatin, it acts as the primary command center of eukaryotic cells. For the point, name this double-membrane-bound organelle that houses genomic DNA.
quizzes.explanation: The cell nucleus is the double-membrane organelle that houses genomic DNA, contains the nucleolus, and regulates eukaryotic cellular activity.

quizzes.question: Its vast drainage basin covers roughly 40 percent of the South American continent and traverses the world's largest tropical rainforest. Extreme seasonal flooding and sparse surrounding infrastructure mean that not a single bridge spans its main stem from its origin in the Andes to its Atlantic delta. It carries more water into the ocean than the next seven largest rivers combined, making up approximately one-fifth of global river discharge. For the point, name this immense South American river second in length only to the Nile.
quizzes.explanation: The Amazon River basin covers 40% of South America, flows through the Amazon Rainforest into the Atlantic, and accounts for ~20% of global river discharge.

quizzes.question: In 1915, Albert Einstein redefined this phenomenon not as a traditional force, but as a geometric consequence of mass and energy warping the fabric of spacetime. Its universal constant, denoted by a capital G, is approximately 6.674 times 10 to the negative 11th power in SI units. Differential interactions from this force between the Earth, Moon, and Sun are directly responsible for ocean tides. For the point, name this fundamental attractive interaction that acts between any two objects with mass, giving Earth's surface an acceleration of 9.81 meters per second squared.
quizzes.explanation: Gravitational force is the fundamental attractive force between masses, governed by Newton's Law of Universal Gravitation and Einstein's General Relativity.

quizzes.question: In 1865, the Royal Geographical Society officially named this peak after a former Surveyor General of India, Sir George Everest. Located in the Mahalangur Himal sub-range, it straddles the border between Nepal and the Tibet Autonomous Region of China at an elevation of over 29,000 feet. Climbers must navigate the dangerous Khumbu Icefall and South Col before entering the Death Zone near its summit. For the point, name this highest mountain peak on Earth.
quizzes.explanation: Mount Everest was named after Sir George Everest in 1865 and is the highest point on Earth, situated in the Mahalangur Himal range.

quizzes.question: These three fundamental principles were first published in 1687 within the groundbreaking treatise Philosophiae Naturalis Principia Mathematica. The first of these principles is commonly called the Law of Inertia, while the third states that whenever one body exerts a force on a second body, an equal and opposite force is exerted in return. The second principle mathematically defines force as the time rate of change of momentum, expressed as F equals m a. For the point, identify these classical mechanics laws named for an English scientist.
quizzes.explanation: Newton's Laws of Motion form the basis of classical mechanics, outlining inertia, F=ma, and equal-and-opposite reaction forces.

quizzes.question: The pororoca is a powerful tidal bore that creates 13-foot-high waves traveling up to 50 miles upstream along this river during full and new moons. Originating high in the Peruvian Andes, this river flows across Peru and Brazil before emptying into the Atlantic Ocean without a single bridge across its main channel. It drains the world's largest tropical rainforest and accounts for roughly 20 percent of all river discharge worldwide. For the point, name this largest river by water volume in the world, located in South America.
quizzes.explanation: The Amazon River flows across South America, experiences the pororoca tidal bore, and discharges more water into the ocean than any other river.

quizzes.question: Within this structure, DNA is wrapped around histone proteins to form chromatin, which condenses into visible chromosomes during cell division. It is enclosed by a nuclear envelope consisting of an inner and outer lipid bilayer separated by the perinuclear space. Containing a prominent sub-region called the nucleolus that synthesizes ribosomal subunits, it acts as the primary control center of eukaryotic cellular function. For the point, name this membrane-bound organelle often referred to as the command center or brain of the cell.
quizzes.explanation: The cell nucleus contains DNA packaged into chromatin by histones, houses the nucleolus, and directs eukaryotic cellular metabolism and reproduction.

quizzes.question: A powerful tidal bore called the pororoca creates waves up to 13 feet high that travel 50 miles upstream along this body of water during full and new moons. Although its traditional source is Nevado Mismi in the Peruvian Andes, recent studies suggest the Mantaro River as its ultimate source, and notably, no bridges cross its main stem due to severe seasonal flooding. Draining roughly 40 percent of South America, it accounts for approximately 20 percent of global river discharge into the oceans. For the point, name this largest river in the world by discharge volume.
quizzes.explanation: The Amazon River is the largest river by discharge volume, featuring no bridges across its main stem, experiencing the pororoca tidal bore, and draining about 40 percent of South America.

quizzes.question: The time rate of change of this physical quantity itself is known in physics as jerk, while its centripetal form maintains circular motion by pointing directly toward the center of curvature. In calculus, this vector quantity is defined as the first derivative of velocity with respect to time and the second derivative of position with respect to time. Under Earth's standard gravity, free-falling objects experience it at approximately 9.81 meters per second squared in the absence of air resistance. For the point, name this rate of change of velocity of an object.
quizzes.explanation: Acceleration is a vector quantity defined as the rate of change of velocity with respect to time. Its derivative is jerk, and standard gravity on Earth causes free-fall acceleration of about 9.81 m/s².

quizzes.question: Continual collision between the Indian and Eurasian tectonic plates causes this geographical feature to grow approximately 4 millimeters higher each year. First confirmed to be summited in 1953 by Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay, climbers attempting it must traverse the Death Zone above 8,000 meters where atmospheric pressure is severely diminished. Known locally as Sagarmatha in Nepal and Chomolungma in Tibet, it was named in 1865 after a former Surveyor General of India. For the point, name this highest mountain above sea level on Earth.
quizzes.explanation: Mount Everest is Earth's highest peak at 8,848.86 meters, situated in the Himalayas on the border of Nepal and Tibet, and was first summited by Hillary and Norgay in 1953.

quizzes.question: The fibrous network supporting the interior of this organelle is called the nuclear lamina, which consists of intermediate filament proteins known as lamins. Within this organelle, ribosomal RNA is transcribed inside a dense sub-structure called the nucleolus, while genomic DNA is complexed with histone proteins to form chromatin. Surrounded by a double-membrane lipid bilayer perforated by nuclear pore complexes, it serves as the primary command center of eukaryotic cells. For the point, name this organelle that houses an organism's genomic DNA.
quizzes.explanation: The cell nucleus is a double-membrane organelle in eukaryotic cells containing genomic DNA, chromatin, the nuclear lamina, and the nucleolus.

quizzes.question: Traversed by zero bridges across its entire main stem, this river's discharge accounts for roughly one-fifth of all river water entering the world's oceans. Its primary source was traditionally identified as Nevado Mismi in Peru, and during full and new moons, it experiences a dramatic tidal bore known as the pororoca. Flowing across South America through the world's largest tropical rainforest, it empties into the Atlantic Ocean. For the point, name this massive river that drains roughly 40 percent of the South American continent.
quizzes.explanation: The Amazon River traverses South America's tropical rainforest, discharging roughly 20 percent of global river flow into the Atlantic Ocean without a single bridge across its main stem.

quizzes.question: In 1915, Albert Einstein redefined this phenomenon not as a traditional force, but as a geometric consequence of mass and energy warping the fabric of spacetime. Its universal constant G is approximately 6.674 times 10 to the negative 11th power, and differential variations in its strength across Earth's surface caused by the Moon and Sun create ocean tides. Sir Isaac Newton formulated a law stating that this attractive interaction is inversely proportional to the square of the distance between two masses. For the point, name this fundamental interaction that pulls objects with mass toward one another.
quizzes.explanation: Gravitational force is an attractive interaction between masses governed by Newton's Law of Universal Gravitation and Einstein's General Theory of Relativity.

quizzes.question: Located in the Mahalangur Himal sub-range of the Himalayas, this peak was officially named in 1865 by the Royal Geographical Society. Near its summit, atmospheric pressure drops dramatically in an area above 8,000 meters known to mountaineers as the Death Zone. Straddling the international border between Nepal and the Tibet Autonomous Region of China, it reaches an elevation of 8,848.86 meters. For the point, name this highest mountain peak in the world.
quizzes.explanation: Mount Everest is located in the Mahalangur Himal sub-range of the Himalayas on the Nepal-China border and is the highest peak on Earth.

quizzes.question: These core physical principles were first published in 1687 in the groundbreaking work Philosophiae Naturalis Principia Mathematica. The second of these principles defines force as the time rate of change of momentum, commonly expressed as net force equals mass times acceleration, while the third states that every action has an equal and opposite reaction. The first of these principles is also known as the Law of Inertia. For the point, identify these three foundational laws of classical mechanics formulated by Sir Isaac Newton.
quizzes.explanation: Newton's Laws of Motion consist of three principles (Inertia, F=ma, Action-Reaction) published in the Principia Mathematica in 1687.

quizzes.question: Surrounding infrastructure is so sparse and seasonal flooding so extreme along this river that not a single bridge spans its entire main stem. The Mantaro River and Nevado Mismi in the Peruvian Andes feed into this body of water, which periodically generates massive tidal waves up to 13 feet high known as pororoca. Draining the world's largest tropical rainforest, it empties into the Atlantic Ocean. For the point, name this second-longest river in the world, located in South America.
quizzes.explanation: The Amazon River flows through South America, fed by Andean tributaries, and holds the title of largest river by volume while lacking any main-stem bridges.

quizzes.question: According to Newton's Second Law of Motion, this vector quantity is directly proportional to net force and inversely proportional to the mass of an object. Its derivative with respect to time is called jerk, and its centripetal form keeps objects moving along a curved path by pointing toward the center of curvature. Measured in standard SI units of meters per second squared, it describes how rapidly an object alters its speed or direction. For the point, name this rate of change of velocity.
quizzes.explanation: Acceleration measures the rate of change of velocity over time, expressed in units of m/s², and relates to force and mass through F = ma.

quizzes.question: In calculus, this quantity represents both the second derivative of position with respect to time and the first derivative of velocity. On Earth's surface, free fall produces a standard value for it of roughly 9.81 meters per second squared. For the point, name this rate of change of velocity.
quizzes.explanation: Acceleration is the time derivative of velocity (a = dv/dt) and equals F/m according to Newton's Second Law of Motion.
